phenomenon-0.title: Hessdalen lights
phenomenon-0.summary: Unexplained floating lights seen in the Hessdalen valley, peaking in 1981-84 at up to 20 per week; an automated scientific station monitors them.
phenomenon-0.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

phenomenon-1.title: Marfa lights
phenomenon-1.summary: Glowing orbs seen near US 67. A 2004 University of Texas study attributed most to vehicle headlights and campfires.
phenomenon-1.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

breakdown: Probable conventional explanation noted by investigators: UT Dallas study: headlights

phenomenon-2.title: Min Min light
phenomenon-2.summary: A light that seems to follow travellers in outback Queensland; a neuroscientist proposed a Fata Morgana inversion mirage.
phenomenon-2.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

breakdown: Partly explained / leading theory accepted by many researchers: Inverted mirage proposed

phenomenon-3.title: Brown Mountain lights
phenomenon-3.summary: Lights over Brown Mountain reported for a century; a 1922 USGS study attributed them to trains and cars.
phenomenon-3.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

breakdown: Probable conventional explanation noted by investigators: USGS: trains and headlights

phenomenon-4.title: Naga fireballs
phenomenon-4.summary: Glowing balls rise from the Mekong each October; a TV investigation suggested tracer rounds fired across the river.
phenomenon-4.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

breakdown: Explanation proposed but disputed: Tracer fire proposed

phenomenon-5.title: Paulding Light
phenomenon-5.summary: A light seen in a valley; Michigan Tech students showed with a telescope that it is car headlights on US 45.
phenomenon-5.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

breakdown: Identified / explained (conventional cause): Car headlights (Michigan Tech, 2010)

phenomenon-6.title: Tunguska event
phenomenon-6.summary: An explosion flattened about 80 million trees over 2,150 km². Most scientists attribute it to the airburst of a stony asteroid or comet.
phenomenon-6.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

breakdown: Partly explained / leading theory accepted by many researchers: Meteoroid airburst (consensus)

images.credit: Leonid Kulik, the expedition to the Tunguska event

rumors.text: A crashing alien spacecraft or a Nikola Tesla energy experiment caused the blast.

phenomenon-7.title: Kentucky meat shower
phenomenon-7.summary: Flakes of meat fell from a clear sky over a 100×50 yard area. The leading explanation is vomit from a flock of vultures.
phenomenon-7.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

breakdown: Probable conventional explanation noted by investigators: Vulture vomit

phenomenon-8.title: Rain of fish (Yoro)
phenomenon-8.summary: Residents report fish found on the ground after storms every year; waterspouts and underground streams are proposed.
phenomenon-8.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

breakdown: Partly explained / leading theory accepted by many researchers: Waterspouts / flooding

phenomenon-9.title: Red rain in Kerala
phenomenon-9.summary: Red-coloured rain fell sporadically for two months. The Indian government study found spores of a lichen-forming alga.
phenomenon-9.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

rumors.text: The red particles were extraterrestrial cells.

phenomenon-10.title: Oakville blobs
phenomenon-10.summary: Gelatinous blobs fell with rain, and residents reported illness. Lab analysis results were inconclusive.
phenomenon-10.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

rumors.text: The blobs were jettisoned aircraft toilet waste.

phenomenon-11.title: Catatumbo lightning
phenomenon-11.summary: Near-continuous lightning over Lake Maracaibo up to 260 nights per year; explained by local winds and topography.
phenomenon-11.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

phenomenon-12.title: Dancing plague of 1518
phenomenon-12.summary: Hundreds of people danced uncontrollably for days. Historians suggest mass psychogenic illness.
phenomenon-12.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

breakdown: Partly explained / leading theory accepted by many researchers: Mass psychogenic illness

rumors.text: Ergot poisoning from moldy rye caused it.

phenomenon-13.title: Tanganyika laughter epidemic
phenomenon-13.summary: Laughter attacks spread from a girls’ boarding school to about 1,000 people; considered mass psychogenic illness.
phenomenon-13.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

breakdown: Partly explained / leading theory accepted by many researchers: Mass psychogenic illness

phenomenon-14.title: Ball lightning spectrum recorded (Qinghai)
phenomenon-14.summary: Chinese scientists recorded the first spectrum of natural ball lightning in 2012 (published 2014), supporting the vaporized-soil hypothesis.
phenomenon-14.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

breakdown: Partly explained / leading theory accepted by many researchers: Soil vapor hypothesis supported

phenomenon-15.title: Earthquake lights (Pisco)
phenomenon-15.summary: Bright luminous flashes filmed during the M8.0 earthquake; earthquake lights are documented but their mechanism is debated.
phenomenon-15.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

breakdown: Partly explained / leading theory accepted by many researchers: Documented, mechanism debated

images.credit: Originally observed and drawn by Friedrich Konzelmann and published in Schmidt, A.; Mack, K. (1912). "Das Süddeutsche Er

phenomenon-16.title: Lake Nyos limnic eruption
phenomenon-16.summary: A sudden release of CO₂ killed about 1,700 people overnight; explained as a limnic eruption.
phenomenon-16.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

phenomenon-17.title: Hornet Spook Light
phenomenon-17.summary: A bouncing light seen on a back road; often attributed to refracted headlights from a highway.
phenomenon-17.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

breakdown: Probable conventional explanation noted by investigators: Refracted headlights

phenomenon-18.title: Day of Darkness (New England)
phenomenon-18.summary: Skies darkened at midday; tree-ring evidence points to massive Canadian wildfires.
phenomenon-18.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.

phenomenon-19.title: Devil’s Footprints
phenomenon-19.summary: Hoof-like tracks ran some 40-100 miles through snow overnight, crossing roofs and walls. Explanations include mice, balloons and hoaxes.
phenomenon-19.license: Summary written for Anomaly Atlas from the linked sources; Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0.
